key_insight: Extending BK19 with two blending switches enables quasi-geostrophic dynamics within the same discretization used for compressible, pseudo-incompressible, and hydrostatic flow.
engineering_relevance: A unified solver can support simulations across atmospheric flow regimes without requiring separate numerical frameworks.
method: Apply small-Rossby-number asymptotic analysis to the fully discrete compressible Euler scheme.
Construct a staggered-grid curl consistent with discrete derivatives to recover the QG pressure Poisson equation.
Add switches for the pressure equation and prognostic versus geostrophically diagnosed horizontal momentum.
evidence_signal: Two idealized vortex tests assess QG vortex stability and show convergence of the compressible scheme toward slow, balanced QG dynamics as the Rossby number decreases.
watch_item: Validation is limited to two idealized vortex cases; performance in complex atmospheric configurations remains unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Access to the quasi-geostrophic model from within the BK19 compressible flow solver
